chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: The Quality Serenaders' lineup after the Cotton Club
summary: Collette reads from an article: Erskine Hawkins, George Orendorff, Lloyd Reese and Charlie Lawrence on reeds, which Howard confirms.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: This is May 22nd, 1978, and we're talking to Paul Howard, with Buddy Collette.

Okay, Paul, a couple of questions here. After the Quality Serenaders left the Cotton Club, it said something about Paul did some reshuffling and added new men. But now some of the people here -- and made some famous Victor recordings -- Tuba Jack was added, and what does it say, I guess Lionel Hampton, Leon Hemford, Louis Taylor, and let's see -- oh, it says something like Louia Taylor left the band of Erskine Hawkins. Now, was it a period when Erskine
Hawkins was in Los Angeles that you knew him as a musician?
Yeah. He got the band and came over to the Quality.
Do you know what band he was with when he came out? He didn't have his own band at that time, did he, Erskine?
No, he came with Erskine Hawkins.
No, I said did Erskine come with another band? Erskine Hawkins.
Yeah, he was in the band. (Inaudible).
Okay. Because it says now George Orrendorf remained, Earl Thompson was added, Lloyd Reese, 'a fine all around musician,' came in on alto.
That's right.
Paul played tenor. Charlie Lawrence joined the reed section on clarinet. Now, this is the same piano player, Charlie Lawrence, right?
Yes.
You forgot to mention to us that he we know was a reed player, see, even though he was a piano player.
He was a reed player.
Well, okay, what came first? Because the only way I knew Charles Lawrence was --
What came first?
-- that he was an outstanding pianist.
See, which you had told us that, because you said Charlie Lawrence was a fine piano player and everything, and you forgot to lay that on us.
I forgot to put that on.

Okay. Good to know, because here's another multiple man like Lloyd Reese who played alto and trumpet and piano and everything. So were there any other players like that that played different instruments?
I can't think of any other. I may come across them in my mind, but I don't know of any others.
Uh-huh.
I sure would let you know.
